note: SEC-EDGE-001. A REASON for every entry in docs/edge-rbac-baseline.json, so "open to all roles" stops reading the same whether an entry is deliberate or unexamined. Verdicts: public (the handler never authenticates, so role is a category error), internal (pg_cron, not a user), headless (nothing calls it, so gating decides nothing — AUDIT-024), open-by-design (every tenant member legitimately uses it; row scoping is the real control), needs-gate (a restriction is wanted and is missing — this is the worklist), unexamined (nobody has looked yet, stated rather than implied). check:edge-rbac requires an entry here for every baselined function.

EXAMINED AND GATED 2026-09-20. An outbound webhook sends this tenant data to a URL the caller chooses, so CREATE is an exfiltration primitive - point it at your own server, subscribe every event - and regenerate-secret breaks whatever live integration verifies signatures with the old one, while test fires a real delivery. All five writes (POST, PUT, test, regenerate-secret, DELETE) now require SUPERVISOR, mirroring the LOWER of the two pages that reach it (/integration-hub 3, /system-integrations 4) so the page at 3 keeps working. Reads stay open and were already safe by construction: every read selects an explicit column list omitting secret, via _shared/webhook-view.ts. Note the inbound receiver POST /api/webhooks/:provider is Express-side and mounted BEFORE the proxy, so none of this touches provider deliveries.
